A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the asymptotic behaviour of the urn model depends on the reducible structure of the Markov chains.
the limiting probability distribution is the unique solution of the fixed point problem and it is Dirichlet if and only if there is a unique recurrent state to which no ball can return.
the limiting frequency distribution is Dirichlet if and only if there is at most one transient state to which returns are not possible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymptotics of the frequencies in a reducible replacement model can be very different from that of a model with a single type of balls.
the limiting probability distribution of the frequencies does not have a product structure in the reducible case.
